| **DR-1403 Dropped Intent Execution Key** | The send intent's dropped intent execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the procedure execution, if the silently dropped flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1404 My Approval Was in Force** | A send intent is flagged my approval was in force only if the send intent is flagged template is sendable. |
| **DR-1405 Refused on Approved Content** | A send intent is flagged refused on approved content if all of the following hold: the my approval was in force flag is set and the content gate passed flag is not set. |
| **DR-1406 Refused on Opt Out Only** | A send intent is flagged refused on opt out only if all of the following hold: the opt out gate passed flag is not set and the length gate passed flag is set. |
| **DR-1407 Refusal Was on My Rules** | A send intent is flagged refusal was on my rules if all of the following hold: the cleared to send flag is not set and at least one of the following holds: the content gate passed flag is not set or the timing gate passed flag is not set. |
| **DR-1408 Refusal Was Outside My Control** | A send intent is flagged refusal was outside my control if all of the following hold: the cleared to send flag is not set and at least one of the following holds: the permission gate passed flag is not set or the authorization gate passed flag is not set. |
| **DR-1409 Is Unreported Refusal on My Rules** | A send intent is considered an unreported refusal on my rules if all of the following hold: the refusal was on my rules flag is set and the approver was notified flag is not set. |
| **DR-1410 Is Approval Overridden Silently** | A send intent is considered an approval overridden silently if all of the following hold: the refused on approved content flag is set and the approver was notified flag is not set. |
| **DR-1411 Has Alternate Channel Attempt** | A send intent is considered to have an alternate channel attempt if the alternate channel intent has a value. |
| **DR-1412 Alternate Attempt Was Cleared** | A send intent's alternate attempt was cleared is true when the send intent's alternate channel intent is a cleared to send. |
| **DR-1413 Is Refused With No Alternative** | A send intent is considered refused-with-no-alternative if all of the following hold: the cleared to send flag is not set and the alternate channel attempt flag is not set. |
| **DR-1414 Exception Prescribed an Alternative** | A send intent is flagged exception prescribed an alternative if all of the following hold: the refusal cited an exception flag is set and the resulting delivery exception has a value. |
| **DR-1415 Prescribed Handling Was Performed** | A send intent is flagged prescribed handling was performed if all of the following hold: the exception prescribed an alternative flag is set and all of the following hold: the alternate channel attempt flag is set and the alternate attempt was cleared flag is set. |
| **DR-1416 Is Suppression Without Remedy** | A send intent is considered suppression-without-remedy if all of the following hold: the exception prescribed an alternative flag is set and the prescribed handling was performed flag is not set. |
| **DR-1417 Has Durable Refusal Record** | A send intent is considered to have a durable refusal record if the refusal recorded at has a value. |
| **DR-1418 Refusal Was Escalated** | A send intent is flagged refusal was escalated if the refusal notified role has a value. |
| **DR-1419 Is Unrecorded Refusal** | A send intent is considered unrecorded-refusal if all of the following hold: the silently dropped flag is set and all of the following hold: the durable refusal record flag is not set and the refusal cited an exception flag is not set. |
| **DR-1420 Is Unescalated Refusal** | A send intent is considered unescalated-refusal if all of the following hold: the cleared to send flag is not set and the refusal was escalated flag is not set. |
| **DR-1421 Unescalated Refusal Role Key** | The send intent's unescalated refusal role key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the refusal notified role, if the unrecorded refusal flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1422 Unrecorded Refusal Execution Key** | The send intent's unrecorded refusal execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the procedure execution, if the unrecorded refusal flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1423 Was Deferred on Timing** | A send intent is considered to have been deferred on timing if all of the following hold: the timing gate passed flag is not set and all of the following hold: the permission gate passed flag is set and the content gate passed flag is set. |
| **DR-1424 As of Instant** | A send intent's as of instant — taken from the linked evaluation context. |
| **DR-1425 Window Has Since Reopened** | A send intent is flagged window has since reopened if all of the following hold: the hours until window opens is greater than 0 and the number of hours from the evaluated at to the as of instant is greater than the hours until window opens. |
| **DR-1426 Has Retry Attempt** | A send intent is considered to have a retry attempt if the retry intent has a value. |
| **DR-1427 Retry Was Cleared** | A send intent's retry was cleared is true when the send intent's retry intent is a cleared to send. |
| **DR-1428 Is Abandoned Deferral** | A send intent is considered abandoned-deferral if all of the following hold: the was deferred on timing flag is set and all of the following hold: the window has since reopened flag is set and the retry attempt flag is not set. |
| **DR-1429 Deferral Age Hours** | A send intent's deferral age hours is computed as the number of hours from the evaluated at to the as of instant. |
| **DR-1430 Is Stale Deferral** | A send intent is considered stale-deferral if all of the following hold: the was deferred on timing flag is set and the deferral age hours is greater than 24. |
| **DR-1431 Enforced by Unauthorized Agent** | A send intent's enforced by unauthorized agent is true when the send intent's evaluating role assignment is an unauthorized enforcement agent. |
| **DR-1432 Consent Input Was Resolvable** | A send intent is flagged consent input was resolvable if the recipient consent status raw has a value. |
| **DR-1433 Recipient Consent Status Raw** | A send intent's recipient consent status raw is the sms consent status of the send intent's recipient. |
| **DR-1434 Policy Input Was Resolvable** | A send intent is flagged policy input was resolvable if the intent policy has a value. |
| **DR-1435 All Gate Inputs Resolved** | A send intent is flagged all gate inputs resolved if all of the following hold: the consent input was resolvable flag is set and the policy input was resolvable flag is set. |
| **DR-1436 Is Unevaluable Refusal** | A send intent is considered unevaluable-refusal if all of the following hold: the cleared to send flag is not set and the all gate inputs resolved flag is not set. |
| **DR-1437 Is Self Witnessed Decision** | A send intent is considered a self witnessed decision if the gate result was independently confirmed flag is not set. |
| **DR-1438 Is Independently Confirmed** | A send intent is considered independently-confirmed if all of the following hold: the resulting delivery flag is set and the resulting delivery was transmitted flag is set. |
| **DR-1439 Independently Confirmed Execution Key** | The send intent's independently confirmed execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the procedure execution, if the independently confirmed flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1440 Name** | An agent decision record's name is computed as the deciding agent, followed by “: ”, followed by the first 60 character(s) of the decision summary. |
| **DR-1441 Was Overridden** | An agent decision record is considered to have been overridden if at least one of the following holds: the human disposition is “Corrected” or the human disposition is “Reversed”. |
| **DR-1442 Was Reviewed** | An agent decision record is considered to have been reviewed if all of the following hold: the human disposition has a value and the human disposition is not “NotReviewed”. |
| **DR-1443 Deciding Agent Kind** | An agent decision record's deciding agent kind — taken from the linked deciding agent. |
| **DR-1444 Deciding Agent When Overridden** | The agent decision record's deciding agent when overridden is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the deciding agent, if the was overridden flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1445 Role Assignment When Scored** | The agent decision record's role assignment when scored is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the under role assignment, if the under role assignment has a value;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1446 Role Assignment When Overridden** | The agent decision record's role assignment when overridden is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the under role assignment, if the was overridden flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1447 Step of Decision** | An agent decision record's step of decision — taken from the linked step execution. |
| **DR-1448 Boundary Match Key** | An agent decision record's boundary match key is computed as the step of decision, followed by “|”, followed by the deciding agent kind, followed by “|”, followed by the decision kind. |
| **DR-1449 Matching Boundary Count** | An agent decision record's matching boundary count is the number of authority boundaries related to the agent decision record. |
| **DR-1450 Violated Authority Boundary** | An agent decision record is flagged violated authority boundary if the matching boundary count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1451 Reviewer Agent Kind** | An agent decision record's reviewer agent kind — taken from the linked reviewed by agent. |
| **DR-1452 Has Human Confirmation** | An agent decision record is considered to have a human confirmation if all of the following hold: the reviewer agent kind is “Human”; the human disposition has a value; and the human disposition is not “NotReviewed”. |
| **DR-1453 Needs Human Confirmation** | An agent decision record is considered to need a human confirmation if all of the following hold: it is not the case that the deciding agent kind is “Human” and at least one of the following holds: the materiality band is “Material” or the materiality band is “Escalated”. |
| **DR-1454 Is Unconfirmed Non Human Decision** | An agent decision record is considered an unconfirmed non human decision if all of the following hold: the needs human confirmation flag is set and the human confirmation flag is not set. |
| **DR-1455 Step Execution When Unconfirmed** | The agent decision record's step execution when unconfirmed is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step execution, if the unconfirmed non human decision flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1456 Agent When Boundary Violated** | The agent decision record's agent when boundary violated is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the deciding agent, if the violated authority boundary flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1457 Review Latency Minutes** | The agent decision record's review latency minutes is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the reviewed at is blank;<br>2. in all other cases, the number of minutes from the decided at to the reviewed at. |
| **DR-1458 Is Draft Kind** | An agent decision record is considered a draft kind if at least one of the following holds: the decision kind is “Draft” or the decision kind is “Commitment”. |
| **DR-1459 Agent When Draft Overridden** | The agent decision record's agent when draft overridden is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the deciding agent, if all of the following hold: the draft kind flag is set and the was overridden flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1460 Agent When Draft** | The agent decision record's agent when draft is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the deciding agent, if the draft kind flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1461 Is Error Correction** | An agent decision record is considered an error correction if all of the following hold: the was overridden flag is set and the override reason kind is “ErrorCorrection”. |
| **DR-1462 Is Reserved Judgment Override** | An agent decision record is considered a reserved judgment override if all of the following hold: the was overridden flag is set and the override reason kind is “JudgmentReserved”. |
| **DR-1463 Override Reason is Recorded** | An agent decision record is flagged override reason is recorded if all of the following hold: the was overridden flag is set and the override reason kind has a value. |
| **DR-1464 Is Unexplained Override** | An agent decision record is considered an unexplained override if all of the following hold: the was overridden flag is set and the override reason is recorded flag is not set. |
| **DR-1465 Error Correction Role Assignment Key** | The agent decision record's error correction role assignment key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the under role assignment, if the error correction flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1466 Boundary Violation Role Assignment Key** | The agent decision record's boundary violation role assignment key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the under role assignment, if the violated authority boundary flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1467 Name** | A delivered communication's name is computed as the channel, followed by “ -> ”, followed by the recipient key, followed by “ @ ”, followed by the sent at. |
| **DR-1468 Has Authorization** | A delivered communication is considered to have an authorization if the authorizing step execution has a value. |
| **DR-1469 Content Matches Approval** | A delivered communication is flagged content matches approval if the rendered content hash is the approved content hash. |
| **DR-1470 Authorized At** | A delivered communication's authorized at is the ended at of the delivered communication's authorizing step execution. |
| **DR-1471 Was Approved Before Sending** | A delivered communication is considered to have been approved before sending if the authorized at is at most the sent at. |
| **DR-1472 Is Defensible** | A delivered communication is considered defensible if all of the following hold: the authorization flag is set; the content matches approval flag is set; and the was approved before sending flag is set. |
| **DR-1473 Name** | An authority boundary's name is computed as the forbidden agent kind, followed by “ may not ”, followed by the forbidden decision kind. |
| **DR-1474 As of Instant** | An authority boundary's as of instant — taken from the linked evaluation context. |
| **DR-1475 Is Currently Binding** | An authority boundary is considered currently-binding if all of the following hold: the status is “Approved”; the valid from is at most the as of instant; and at least one of the following holds: the valid to is blank or the valid to is greater than the as of instant. |
| **DR-1476 Ratifying Fragment is Valid** | An authority boundary's ratifying fragment is valid is true when the authority boundary's ratified by knowledge fragment is currently valid. |
| **DR-1477 Step When Binding** | The authority boundary's step when binding is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the currently binding flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1478 Boundary Match Key** | An authority boundary's boundary match key is computed as the step, followed by “|”, followed by the forbidden agent kind, followed by “|”, followed by the forbidden decision kind. |
| **DR-1479 Violation Count** | An authority boundary's violation count is the number of agent decision records related to the authority boundary. |
| **DR-1480 Is Untested** | An authority boundary is considered untested if all of the following hold: the currently binding flag is set and the violation count is 0. |
| **DR-1481 Has Ratifying Fragment** | An authority boundary is considered to have ratifying fragment if the ratified by knowledge fragment has a value. |
| **DR-1482 Is Unwarranted** | An authority boundary is considered unwarranted if all of the following hold: the currently binding flag is set and at least one of the following holds: the ratifying fragment flag is not set or the ratifying fragment is valid flag is not set. |
| **DR-1483 Ratifying Fragment is Overdue** | An authority boundary's ratifying fragment is overdue is true when the authority boundary's ratified by knowledge fragment is an overdue for review. |
| **DR-1484 Ratifying Fragment is Single Witness** | An authority boundary's ratifying fragment is single witness is true when the authority boundary's ratified by knowledge fragment is a from single witness. |
| **DR-1485 Warrant is Thin** | An authority boundary is flagged warrant is thin if all of the following hold: the currently binding flag is set and at least one of the following holds: the ratifying fragment is overdue flag is set or the ratifying fragment is single witness flag is set. |
| **DR-1486 Is Unwarranted and Untested** | An authority boundary is considered unwarranted-and-untested if all of the following hold: the unwarranted flag is set and the untested flag is set. |
| **DR-1487 Unwarranted Boundary Step Key** | The authority boundary's unwarranted boundary step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the unwarranted flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1488 Ratifying Fragment Key** | The authority boundary's ratifying fragment key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the ratified by knowledge fragment, if the currently binding flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1489 Ratifying Fragment Status** | An authority boundary's ratifying fragment status — taken from the linked ratified by knowledge fragment. |
| **DR-1490 Ratification Lapsed** | An authority boundary is flagged ratification lapsed if all of the following hold: the ratifying fragment flag is set and the ratifying fragment is valid flag is not set. |
| **DR-1491 Binds Despite Lapsed Ratification** | An authority boundary is considered to bind a despite lapsed ratification if all of the following hold: the currently binding flag is set and the ratification lapsed flag is set. |
| **DR-1492 Is Ungrounded and Untested** | An authority boundary is considered ungrounded-and-untested if all of the following hold: the binds despite lapsed ratification flag is set and the untested flag is set. |
| **DR-1493 Constrained Role Assignment Key** | The authority boundary's constrained role assignment key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the authority role, if the binds despite lapsed ratification flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1494 Name** | A binding observation's name is computed as the step execution, followed by “ / ”, followed by the binding observation ID. |
| **DR-1495 Sla Minutes At Run** | A binding observation's sla minutes at run is the freshness sla minutes of the binding observation's operational binding. |
| **DR-1496 Age At Run Minutes** | A binding observation's age at run minutes is computed as the number of minutes from the observed source timestamp to the read at. |
| **DR-1497 Was Stale At Run** | A binding observation is considered to have been stale at run if all of the following hold: the authoritative binding flag is set and the age at run minutes is greater than the sla minutes at run. |
| **DR-1498 Is Authoritative Binding** | A binding observation's is authoritative binding when the linked operational binding is authoritative. |
| **DR-1499 Stale At Run Step Key** | The binding observation's stale at run step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step execution, if the was stale at run flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1500 Name** | An attestation's name is computed as the procedure execution, followed by “ / ”, followed by the attestation ID. |
| **DR-1501 Version is Fit Now** | An attestation's version is fit now is true when the attestation's procedure execution is a fit. |
| **DR-1502 Fitness Verdict Has Drifted** | An attestation is considered to fitnes verdict has drifted if it is not the case that the version was fit at signing is the version is fit now. |
| **DR-1503 Assurance Grade Now** | An attestation's assurance grade now — taken from the linked procedure execution. |
| **DR-1504 Assurance Grade Has Drifted** | An attestation is flagged assurance grade has drifted if it is not the case that the assurance grade at signing is the assurance grade now. |
| **DR-1505 Would Not Survive Restatement** | An attestation is flagged would not survive restatement if at least one of the following holds: the fitness verdict has drifted flag is set or the assurance grade has drifted flag is set. |
| **DR-1506 Name** | An app role profile's name is computed as the display label, followed by “ (”, followed by the role kind, followed by “)”. |
| **DR-1507 Route Count** | An app role profile's route count is the number of app routes related to the app role profile. |
| **DR-1508 Name** | An app nav group's name is the same as its group label. |
| **DR-1509 Route Count** | An app nav group's route count is the number of app routes related to the app nav group. |
| **DR-1510 Name** | An app route's name is computed as the route name, followed by “ — ”, followed by the route path. |
| **DR-1511 Is in Nav** | An app route is considered in-nav if the nav group has a value. |
| **DR-1512 Is Shared** | An app route is considered shared if all of the following hold: the owning role is blank and the surface is “domain”. |
| **DR-1513 Is Maintainer** | An app route is considered a maintainer if the surface is “maintainer”. |
| **DR-1514 Question Count** | An app route's question count is the number of app route questions related to the app route. |
| **DR-1515 Reference Count** | An app route's reference count is the number of app route references related to the app route. |
| **DR-1516 Answers No Question** | An app route is considered to answer no question if all of the following hold: the question count is 0; the is shared is false; the is maintainer is false; and the route kind is not “index”. |
| **DR-1517 Name** | An app route question's name is computed as the route, followed by “ answers ”, followed by the question. |
| **DR-1518 Name** | An app route reference's name is computed as the from route, followed by “ -> ”, followed by the to route. |
| **DR-1519 Name** | A rulebook table's name is the same as its table name. |
| **DR-1520 Field Count** | A rulebook table's field count is the number of rulebook fields related to the rulebook table. |
| **DR-1521 Policy Count** | A rulebook table's policy count is the number of access policies related to the rulebook table. |
| **DR-1522 Is Unsecured** | A rulebook table is considered unsecured if the policy count is 0. |
| **DR-1523 Disagreeing Substrate Count** | A rulebook table's disagreeing substrate count is the number of table conformance related to the rulebook table. |
| **DR-1524 Has Measured Rows** | A rulebook table is considered to have a measured rows if the measured row count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1525 Semantic Mapping Count** | A rulebook table's semantic mapping count is the number of semantic mappings related to the rulebook table. |
| **DR-1526 Meaning is Only Tabular** | A rulebook table is flagged meaning is only tabular if the semantic mapping count is 0. |
| **DR-1527 Exact Mapping Count** | A rulebook table's exact mapping count is the number of the rulebook table's semantic mappings that have a mapping relation of “exact”. |
| **DR-1528 Aligned Mapping Count** | A rulebook table's aligned mapping count is the number of the rulebook table's semantic mappings that have a mapping relation of “aligned”. |
| **DR-1529 Is Unaligned to Standard** | A rulebook table is considered an unaligned to standard if the exact mapping count plus the aligned mapping count is 0. |
| **DR-1530 Semantic Type Iri Field Count** | A rulebook table's semantic type iri field count is the number of the rulebook table's rulebook fields that have a field name of “SemanticTypeIri”. |
| **DR-1531 Lacks Semantic Type Convention** | A rulebook table is considered to lack a semantic type convention if the semantic type iri field count is 0. |
| **DR-1532 Is Unsecured Governance Record** | A rulebook table is considered an unsecured governance record if all of the following hold: the subject area is “governance” and the policy count is 0. |
| **DR-1533 Unrestricted Non Admin Policy Count** | A rulebook table's unrestricted non admin policy count is the number of the rulebook table's access policies that are unrestricted-non-admin-grant. |
| **DR-1534 Restricted Non Admin Policy Count** | A rulebook table's restricted non admin policy count is the number of the rulebook table's access policies that are not unrestricted-non-admin-grant and are not principal is admin. |
| **DR-1535 Is Readable in Full by Non Admin** | A rulebook table is considered a readable in full by non admin if the unrestricted non admin policy count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1536 Is Controlled for Every Non Admin** | A rulebook table is considered a controlled for every non admin if all of the following hold: the restricted non admin policy count is greater than 0 and the unrestricted non admin policy count is 0. |
| **DR-1537 Name** | An access principal's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1538 Organization Scope** | An access principal's organization scope — taken from the linked domain role. |
| **DR-1539 Role Label** | An access principal's role label — taken from the linked domain role. |
| **DR-1540 Policy Count** | An access principal's policy count is the number of access policies related to the access principal. |
| **DR-1541 Grant Count** | An access principal's grant count is the number of field grants related to the access principal. |
| **DR-1542 Visible Table Count** | An access principal's visible table count is the number of role schema views related to the access principal. |
| **DR-1543 Has No Access** | An access principal is considered to have no access if the policy count is 0. |
| **DR-1544 Is Over Privileged** | An access principal is considered over-privileged if all of the following hold: the administrator flag is not set and the visible table count is at least 74. |
| **DR-1545 Name** | An access policy's name is computed as the principal, followed by a space, followed by the command, followed by a space, followed by the target table. |
| **DR-1546 Is Write Command** | An access policy is considered a write command if at least one of the following holds: the command is “INSERT”; the command is “UPDATE”; the command is “DELETE”; or the command is “ALL”. |
| **DR-1547 Is Unrestricted** | An access policy is considered unrestricted if the row predicate is blank. |
| **DR-1548 Principal is Admin** | An access policy's principal is admin is true when the access policy's principal is an administrator. |
| **DR-1549 Is Unrestricted Non Admin Grant** | An access policy is considered unrestricted-non-admin-grant if all of the following hold: the unrestricted flag is set and the principal is admin flag is not set. |
| **DR-1550 Is Unwitnessed Write** | An access policy is considered an unwitnessed write if all of the following hold: the write command flag is set and the denial test count is 0. |
| **DR-1551 Denial Test Count** | An access policy's denial test count is the number of access denial tests related to the access policy. |
| **DR-1552 Name** | A field grant's name is computed as the principal, followed by “ -> ”, followed by the target field. |
| **DR-1553 Field Table** | A field grant's field table is the target table of the field grant's target field. |
| **DR-1554 Field Name** | A field grant's field name — taken from the linked target field. |
| **DR-1555 Field is Derived** | A field grant's field is derived when the linked target field is derived. |
| **DR-1556 Is Writable Derived Field** | A field grant is considered a writable derived field if all of the following hold: the can write flag is set and the field is derived flag is set. |
| **DR-1557 Is Masked** | A field grant is considered masked if all of the following hold: the mask strategy is not “plain” and the mask strategy has a value. |
| **DR-1558 Grant Key When Readable** | The field grant's grant key when readable is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the principal, followed by “|”, followed by the field table, if the can read flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1559 Name** | A role schema's name is the same as its schema name. |
| **DR-1560 Search Path** | A role schema's search path is the same as its schema name. |
| **DR-1561 View Count** | A role schema's view count is the number of role schema views related to the role schema. |
| **DR-1562 Is Empty Schema** | A role schema is considered an empty schema if the view count is 0. |
| **DR-1563 Name** | A role schema view's name is computed as the schema name, followed by a period, followed by the view name. |
| **DR-1564 Schema Name** | A role schema view's schema name — taken from the linked role schema. |
| **DR-1565 Source View** | A role schema view's source view is the physical view of the role schema view's target table. |
| **DR-1566 Grant Key** | A role schema view's grant key is computed as the principal, followed by “|”, followed by the target table. |
| **DR-1567 Column Count** | A role schema view's column count is the number of field grants related to the role schema view. |
| **DR-1568 Table Field Count** | A role schema view's table field count — taken from the linked target table. |
| **DR-1569 Is Full Width** | A role schema view is considered a full width if all of the following hold: the column count is greater than 0 and the column count is at least the table field count. |
| **DR-1570 Is Degenerate View** | A role schema view is considered a degenerate view if the column count is 0. |
| **DR-1571 Name** | A jwt claim mapping's name is computed as the claim name, followed by “ -> ”, followed by the SQL accessor. |
| **DR-1572 Usage Count** | A jwt claim mapping's usage count is the number of access policies related to the jwt claim mapping. |
| **DR-1573 Name** | An access denial test's name is computed as the principal, followed by “ must not see ”, followed by the forbidden row ID. |
| **DR-1574 Has Run** | An access denial test is considered to have a run if the last run at has a value. |
| **DR-1575 Is Passing** | An access denial test is considered passing if the observed visible is the expected visible. |
| **DR-1576 Is Leak** | An access denial test is considered a leak if all of the following hold: the expected visible flag is not set and the observed visible flag is set. |
| **DR-1577 Is Unproven** | An access denial test is considered an unproven if the run flag is not set. |
| **DR-1578 Is Positive Control** | An access denial test is considered a positive control only if the access denial test is flagged expected visible. |
| **DR-1579 Name** | An app user's name is the same as its display name. |
| **DR-1580 Agent Kind** | An app user's agent kind — taken from the linked linked agent. |
| **DR-1581 Organization** | An app user's organization — taken from the linked linked agent. |
| **DR-1582 Assignment Count** | An app user's assignment count is the number of principal assignments related to the app user. |
| **DR-1583 Has No Principal** | An app user is considered to have no principal if the assignment count is 0. |
| **DR-1584 Holds Multiple Principals** | An app user is considered to hold a multiple principals if the assignment count is greater than 1. |
| **DR-1585 Is Non Human Sign in** | An app user is considered a non human sign in if at least one of the following holds: the agent kind is “AIAgent” or the agent kind is “AutomatedPipeline”. |
| **DR-1586 Name** | A principal assignment's name is computed as the app user, followed by “ as ”, followed by the principal. |
| **DR-1587 Principal is Admin** | A principal assignment's principal is admin is true when the principal assignment's principal is an administrator. |
| **DR-1588 User Organization** | A principal assignment's user organization — taken from the linked app user. |
| **DR-1589 Principal Organization** | A principal assignment's principal organization is the organization scope of the principal assignment's principal. |
| **DR-1590 Is Cross Organization Grant** | A principal assignment is considered cross-organization-grant if all of the following hold: the user organization has a value; the principal organization has a value; and the user organization is not the principal organization. |
| **DR-1591 Name** | An issued token's name is computed as the app user, followed by “ as ”, followed by the principal, followed by “ @ ”, followed by the issued at. |
| **DR-1592 Is Dev Minted** | An issued token is considered dev-minted if the issuer is “dev-mint”. |
| **DR-1593 Name** | A process mining run's name is computed as the event log source, followed by “ / ”, followed by the mined at. |
| **DR-1594 As of Instant** | A process mining run's as of instant — taken from the linked evaluation context. |
| **DR-1595 Conformance Rate** | The process mining run's conformance rate is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the discovered variant count is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, the conforming variant count divided by the discovered variant count. |
| **DR-1596 Is Conformant** | A process mining run is considered conformant if the conformance rate is at least 0.8. |
| **DR-1597 Has Major Drift From Documentation** | A process mining run is considered to have a major drift from documentation if the conformance rate is less than 0.5. |
| **DR-1598 Days Since Mined** | A process mining run's days since mined is computed as the number of days from the mined at to the as of instant. |
| **DR-1599 Is Stale Mining Evidence** | A process mining run is considered a stale mining evidence if the days since mined is greater than 180. |
| **DR-1600 Procedure Version is Live** | A process mining run's procedure version is live when the linked procedure version is live. |
| **DR-1601 Is Drift on Live Version** | A process mining run is considered a drift on live version if all of the following hold: the major drift from documentation flag is set and the procedure version is live flag is set. |
| **DR-1602 Drifted Mining Run Key** | The process mining run's drifted mining run key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the procedure version, if the drift on live version flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1603 People Capture Complement Count** | A process mining run's people capture complement count is the number of the process mining run's collected source materials that hold a reasoning or tacit knowledge. |
| **DR-1604 Is Deviation Unexplained by People** | A process mining run is considered a deviation unexplained by people if all of the following hold: the discovered variant count is greater than the conforming variant count and the people capture complement count is 0. |
| **DR-1605 Undocumented Path Count** | A process mining run's undocumented path count is the number of the process mining run's mined flow edges that are undocumented paths. |
| **DR-1606 Has Undocumented Enacted Path** | A process mining run is considered to have an undocumented enacted path if the undocumented path count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1607 Conformance Percent** | A process mining run's conformance percent is computed as the conformance rate times 100 rounded to 0 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1608 Name** | A vocabulary's name is the same as its title. |
| **DR-1609 Term Count** | A vocabulary's term count is the number of vocabulary terms related to the vocabulary. |
| **DR-1610 Orphan Term Count** | A vocabulary's orphan term count is the number of vocabulary terms related to the vocabulary. |
| **DR-1611 Has Orphan Terms** | A vocabulary is considered to have an orphan terms if the orphan term count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1612 Is Machine Accessible** | A vocabulary is considered machine-accessible if all of the following hold: the scheme uri has a value and the publication format is “SKOS Turtle”. |
| **DR-1613 Managed Scheme Procedure Key** | The vocabulary's managed scheme procedure key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the governs procedure, if all of the following hold: the governing role has a value and the established at has a value;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1614 Organized Transcript Count** | A vocabulary's organized transcript count is the number of the vocabulary's collected source materials that have a material kind of “Transcript”. |
| **DR-1615 Organized Field Notes Count** | A vocabulary's organized field notes count is the number of the vocabulary's collected source materials that have a material kind of “FieldNotes”. |
| **DR-1616 Organized Process Map Count** | A vocabulary's organized process map count is the number of the vocabulary's collected source materials that have a material kind of “ProcessMap”. |
| **DR-1617 Organized Mined Event Trace Count** | A vocabulary's organized mined event trace count is the number of the vocabulary's collected source materials that have a material kind of “MinedEventTrace”. |
| **DR-1618 Organized Document Excerpt Count** | A vocabulary's organized document excerpt count is the number of the vocabulary's collected source materials that have a material kind of “DocumentExcerpt”. |
| **DR-1619 Organized Material Count** | A vocabulary's organized material count is the number of collected source materials related to the vocabulary. |
| **DR-1620 Organized Kind Count** | A vocabulary's organized kind count is computed as the count of the following that hold: the organized transcript count is greater than 0; the organized field notes count is greater than 0; the organized process map count is greater than 0; the organized mined event trace count is greater than 0; and the organized document excerpt count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1621 Is Single Kind Frame** | A vocabulary is considered a single kind frame if all of the following hold: the organized material count is at least 2 and the organized kind count is 1. |
| **DR-1622 Latest Organized Material At** | A vocabulary's latest organized material at is the largest collected at across the collected source materials related to the vocabulary. |
| **DR-1623 Refinement Count** | A vocabulary's refinement count is the number of scheme refinements related to the vocabulary. |
| **DR-1624 Is Frozen Despite New Collection** | A vocabulary is considered a frozen despite new collection if all of the following hold: the established at has a value; the latest organized material at has a value; the latest organized material at is greater than the established at; and the refinement count is 0. |
| **DR-1625 Ontology Preceded Vocabulary Control** | A vocabulary is flagged ontology preceded vocabulary control if all of the following hold: the ontology modeling started at has a value and at least one of the following holds: the established at is blank or the ontology modeling started at is less than the established at. |
| **DR-1626 Name** | A vocabulary term's name is the same as its pref label. |
| **DR-1627 Usage Count** | A vocabulary term's usage count is the number of requirements related to the vocabulary term. |
| **DR-1628 Is Orphan Term** | A vocabulary term is considered an orphan term if the usage count is 0. |
| **DR-1629 Is Widely Adopted Term** | A vocabulary term is considered a widely adopted term if the usage count is at least 2. |
| **DR-1630 Orphan Term Vocabulary Key** | The vocabulary term's orphan term vocabulary key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the vocabulary, if the orphan term flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1631 Broader Term Parent** | A vocabulary term's broader term parent — taken from the linked broader term. |
| **DR-1632 Scheme Governed Dimension** | A vocabulary term's scheme governed dimension — taken from the linked vocabulary. |
| **DR-1633 Introduced Release Issued At** | A vocabulary term's introduced release issued at — taken from the linked introduced in release. |
| **DR-1634 Latest Meaning Change At** | A vocabulary term's latest meaning change at is the largest changed at across the term meaning changes related to the vocabulary term. |
| **DR-1635 Has Stale Definition** | A vocabulary term is considered to have a stale definition if all of the following hold: the latest meaning change at has a value and at least one of the following holds: the definition revised at is blank or the definition revised at is less than the latest meaning change at. |
| **DR-1636 Structural Shift Count** | A vocabulary term's structural shift count is the number of the vocabulary term's term meaning changes that are structural changes and have a span days of “>=700”. |
| **DR-1637 Has Structural Sense Shift Across Years** | A vocabulary term is considered to have a structural sense shift across years if the structural shift count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1638 Pref Label Practitioner Mention Count** | A vocabulary term's pref label practitioner mention count is the total practitioner mention count across the vocabulary term's term label variants that have a label kind of “pref”. |
| **DR-1639 Alt Label Practitioner Mention Count** | A vocabulary term's alt label practitioner mention count is the total practitioner mention count across the vocabulary term's term label variants that have a label kind of “alt”. |
| **DR-1640 Is Organized Around Official Term** | A vocabulary term is considered an organized around official term if all of the following hold: the alt label practitioner mention count is at least 2 and the alt label practitioner mention count is greater than the pref label practitioner mention count. |
| **DR-1641 Source Phrasing Count** | A vocabulary term's source phrasing count is the number of source term mentions related to the vocabulary term. |
| **DR-1642 Unreconciled Phrasing Count** | A vocabulary term's unreconciled phrasing count is the number of source term mentions related to the vocabulary term. |
| **DR-1643 Has Unreconciled Variant Phrasings** | A vocabulary term is considered to have an unreconciled variant phrasings if all of the following hold: the source phrasing count is at least 2 and the unreconciled phrasing count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1644 Name** | A knowledge broker link's name is computed as the seeker, followed by “ -> ”, followed by the broker. |
| **DR-1645 As of Instant** | A knowledge broker link's as of instant — taken from the linked evaluation context. |
| **DR-1646 Days Since Consulted** | A knowledge broker link's days since consulted is computed as the number of days from the last consulted at to the as of instant. |
| **DR-1647 Is Active Reliance** | A knowledge broker link is considered an active reliance if all of the following hold: it is not the case that the frequency is “Rarely” and the days since consulted is at most 180. |
| **DR-1648 Broker is Still Engaged** | A knowledge broker link's broker is still engaged when the linked broker is still engaged. |
| **DR-1649 Is At Risk Reliance** | A knowledge broker link is considered at-risk-reliance if all of the following hold: the active reliance flag is set and the broker is still engaged flag is not set. |
| **DR-1650 Active Reliance Broker Key** | The knowledge broker link's active reliance broker key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the broker, if the active reliance flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1651 At Risk Broker Key** | The knowledge broker link's at risk broker key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the broker, if the at risk reliance flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1652 Pointed Holder** | A knowledge broker link's pointed holder is the holder agent of the knowledge broker link's points to know how. |
| **DR-1653 Locates Other Holder** | A knowledge broker link is considered to locate an other holder if all of the following hold: the points to know how has a value; the pointed holder has a value; and the pointed holder is not the broker. |
| **DR-1654 Translation Between Vocabularies** | The knowledge broker link's translation between vocabularies is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the seeker wording, followed by “ (”, followed by the seeker vocabulary, followed by “) = ”, followed by the holder wording, followed by “ (”, followed by the holder vocabulary, followed by “)”, if all of the following hold: the seeker vocabulary has a value; the holder vocabulary has a value; and the seeker vocabulary is not the holder vocabulary;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1655 Name** | A conformance substrate's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1656 Is Graded** | A conformance substrate is considered graded if the role is “graded”. |
| **DR-1657 Run Count** | A conformance substrate's run count is the number of substrate run scores related to the conformance substrate. |
| **DR-1658 Latest Cells Tested** | A conformance substrate's latest cells tested is the total latest cells tested across the substrate run scores related to the conformance substrate. |
| **DR-1659 Latest Cells Passed** | A conformance substrate's latest cells passed is the total latest cells passed across the substrate run scores related to the conformance substrate. |
| **DR-1660 Latest Harness Errors** | A conformance substrate's latest harness errors is the total latest error flag across the substrate run scores related to the conformance substrate. |
| **DR-1661 Latest Cells Failed** | A conformance substrate's latest cells failed is computed as the latest cells tested minus the latest cells passed. |
| **DR-1662 Latest Score** | The conformance substrate's latest score is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the latest cells tested is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the latest cells passed divided by the latest cells tested rounded to 2 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1663 Disagreeing Field Count** | A conformance substrate's disagreeing field count is the number of field disagreements related to the conformance substrate. |
| **DR-1664 Disagreeing Table Count** | A conformance substrate's disagreeing table count is the number of table conformance related to the conformance substrate. |
| **DR-1665 Is Fully Conformant** | A conformance substrate is considered fully-conformant if all of the following hold: the latest cells tested is greater than 0; the latest cells failed is 0; and the latest harness errors is 0. |
| **DR-1666 Name** | A conformance run's name is the same as its conformance run ID. |
| **DR-1667 Substrate Count** | A conformance run's substrate count is the number of substrate run scores related to the conformance run. |
| **DR-1668 Perfect Substrate Count** | A conformance run's perfect substrate count is the number of substrate run scores related to the conformance run. |
| **DR-1669 Cells Tested** | A conformance run's cells tested is the total cells tested across the substrate run scores related to the conformance run. |
| **DR-1670 Cells Passed** | A conformance run's cells passed is the total cells passed across the substrate run scores related to the conformance run. |
| **DR-1671 Cells Failed** | A conformance run's cells failed is computed as the cells tested minus the cells passed. |
| **DR-1672 Overall Score** | The conformance run's overall score is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the cells tested is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the cells passed divided by the cells tested rounded to 2 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1673 Imperfect Substrate Count** | A conformance run's imperfect substrate count is computed as the substrate count minus the perfect substrate count. |
| **DR-1674 Is Fully Conformant** | A conformance run is considered fully-conformant if all of the following hold: the substrate count is greater than 0 and the imperfect substrate count is 0. |
| **DR-1675 Name** | A substrate run score's name is computed as the run, followed by “ / ”, followed by the substrate. |
| **DR-1676 Cells Failed** | A substrate run score's cells failed is computed as the cells tested minus the cells passed. |
| **DR-1677 Score** | The substrate run score's score is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the cells tested is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the cells passed divided by the cells tested rounded to 2 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1678 Calculated Score** | The substrate run score's calculated score is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the calculated tested is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the calculated passed divided by the calculated tested rounded to 2 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1679 Lookup Score** | The substrate run score's lookup score is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the lookup tested is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the lookup passed divided by the lookup tested rounded to 2 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1680 Aggregation Score** | The substrate run score's aggregation score is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the aggregation tested is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the aggregation passed divided by the aggregation tested rounded to 2 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1681 Is Perfect** | A substrate run score is considered a perfect if all of the following hold: the harness error is blank; the cells tested is greater than 0; and the cells failed is 0. |
| **DR-1682 Perfect Run Key** | The substrate run score's perfect run key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the run, if the perfect flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1683 Is in Latest Run** | A substrate run score's is in latest run when the linked run is a latest. |
| **DR-1684 Latest Cells Tested** | The substrate run score's latest cells tested is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the cells tested, if the in latest run flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, 0. |
| **DR-1685 Latest Cells Passed** | The substrate run score's latest cells passed is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the cells passed, if the in latest run flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, 0. |
| **DR-1686 Latest Error Flag** | The substrate run score's latest error flag is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 1, if all of the following hold: the in latest run flag is set and the harness error has a value;<br>2. in all other cases, 0. |
| **DR-1687 Substrate Label** | A substrate run score's substrate label — taken from the linked substrate. |
| **DR-1688 Name** | A table conformance's name is computed as the substrate, followed by “ / ”, followed by the rulebook table. |
| **DR-1689 Cells Failed** | A table conformance's cells failed is computed as the cells tested minus the cells passed. |
| **DR-1690 Score** | The table conformance's score is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the cells tested is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the cells passed divided by the cells tested rounded to 2 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1691 Is Perfect** | A table conformance is considered a perfect if the cells failed is 0. |
| **DR-1692 Imperfect Substrate Key** | The table conformance's imperfect substrate key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. an empty string, if the perfect flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, the substrate. |
| **DR-1693 Imperfect Table Key** | The table conformance's imperfect table key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. an empty string, if the perfect flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, the rulebook table. |
| **DR-1694 Disagreeing Field Count** | A table conformance's disagreeing field count is the number of field disagreements related to the table conformance. |
| **DR-1695 Substrate Label** | A table conformance's substrate label — taken from the linked substrate. |
| **DR-1696 Subject Area** | A table conformance's subject area — taken from the linked rulebook table. |
| **DR-1697 Name** | A field disagreement's name is computed as the substrate, followed by “ / ”, followed by the rulebook field. |
| **DR-1698 Sampled Cell Count** | A field disagreement's sampled cell count is the number of cell disagreements related to the field disagreement. |
| **DR-1699 Is Fully Sampled** | A field disagreement is considered fully-sampled if the sampled cell count is the cells failed. |
| **DR-1700 Formula** | A field disagreement's formula — taken from the linked rulebook field. |
| **DR-1701 Substrate Label** | A field disagreement's substrate label — taken from the linked substrate. |
| **DR-1702 Name** | A cell disagreement's name is computed as the field disagreement, followed by “ @ ”, followed by the record ID. |
| **DR-1703 Substrate** | A cell disagreement's substrate — taken from the linked field disagreement. |
| **DR-1704 Rulebook Field** | A cell disagreement's rulebook field — taken from the linked field disagreement. |
| **DR-1705 Name** | A knowledge method's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1706 Elicitation Use Count** | A knowledge method's elicitation use count is the number of elicitation sessions related to the knowledge method. |
| **DR-1707 Application Count** | A knowledge method's application count is the number of method applications related to the knowledge method. |
| **DR-1708 Usage Count** | A knowledge method's usage count is computed as the elicitation use count plus the application count. |
| **DR-1709 Is Applied** | A knowledge method is considered applied if the usage count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1710 Name** | A source article's name is the same as its title. |
| **DR-1711 Claim Count** | A source article's claim count is the number of article claims related to the source article. |
| **DR-1712 Covered Claim Count** | A source article's covered claim count is the number of the source article's article claims that are covered. |
| **DR-1713 Agreed Claim Count** | A source article's agreed claim count is the number of the source article's article claims that are agreed. |
| **DR-1714 Uncovered Claim Count** | A source article's uncovered claim count is computed as the claim count minus the covered claim count. |
| **DR-1715 Coverage Percent** | The source article's coverage percent is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the claim count is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the covered claim count divided by the claim count rounded to 1 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1716 Agreed Coverage Percent** | The source article's agreed coverage percent is determined by the following priority:<br>1. 0, if the claim count is 0;<br>2. in all other cases, 100 times the agreed claim count divided by the claim count rounded to 1 decimal place(s). |
| **DR-1717 Is Fully Covered** | A source article is considered fully-covered if all of the following hold: the claim count is greater than 0 and the uncovered claim count is 0. |
| **DR-1718 Name** | An article claim's name is computed as the article claim ID, followed by “: ”, followed by the first 60 character(s) of the claim text. |
| **DR-1719 Required Evidence** | The article claim's required evidence is determined by the following priority:<br>1. “a table with rows or a field with data”, if the claim kind is “Concept”;<br>2. “an answered role question with a computed answer”, if the claim kind is “CompetencyQuestion”;<br>3. “a mapped ontology profile or an applied knowledge method”, if the claim kind is “Standard”;<br>4. “a procedure with recorded executions”, if the claim kind is “Scenario”;<br>5. in all other cases, “a discriminating witness invented for a role question”. |
| **DR-1720 Evidence Count** | An article claim's evidence count is the number of claim evidence related to the article claim. |
| **DR-1721 Valid Evidence Count** | An article claim's valid evidence count is the number of the article claim's claim evidence that are valid. |
| **DR-1722 Agreed Evidence Count** | An article claim's agreed evidence count is the number of the article claim's claim evidence that are agreed evidences. |
| **DR-1723 Is Covered** | An article claim is considered covered if the valid evidence count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1724 Is Agreed** | An article claim is considered agreed if the agreed evidence count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1725 Has Rejected Evidence** | An article claim is considered to have a rejected evidence if all of the following hold: the evidence count is greater than 0 and the valid evidence count is 0. |
| **DR-1726 Name** | A claim evidence's name is computed as the article claim, followed by “ <- ”, followed by the evidence kind. |
| **DR-1727 Claim Kind** | A claim evidence's claim kind — taken from the linked article claim. |
| **DR-1728 Field Catalog Name** | A claim evidence's field catalog name — taken from the linked rulebook field. |
| **DR-1729 Field is Witness** | A claim evidence's field is witness is true when the claim evidence's rulebook field is a witness. |
| **DR-1730 Field Has Data** | A claim evidence's field has data is true when the claim evidence's rulebook field has a measured data. |
| **DR-1731 Field is Discriminating** | A claim evidence's field is discriminating when the linked rulebook field is discriminating. |
| **DR-1732 Field is Contested** | A claim evidence's field is contested is true when the claim evidence's rulebook field is substrate contested. |
| **DR-1733 Table Has Rows** | A claim evidence's table has rows is true when the claim evidence's rulebook table has a measured rows. |
| **DR-1734 Question is Answered** | A claim evidence's question is answered when the linked role question is answered. |
| **DR-1735 Question Witnessed Answer** | A claim evidence's question witnessed answer — taken from the linked role question. |
| **DR-1736 Profile Mapping Count** | A claim evidence's profile mapping count — taken from the linked ontology profile. |
| **DR-1737 Method is Applied** | A claim evidence's method is applied when the linked knowledge method is applied. |
| **DR-1738 Procedure Execution Count** | A claim evidence's procedure execution count — taken from the linked procedure. |
| **DR-1739 Has Justification** | A claim evidence is considered to have a justification if the justification has a value. |
| **DR-1740 Is Witness Proof** | A claim evidence is considered a witness proof if all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “Field”; the field catalog name has a value; the field is witness flag is set; and the field is discriminating flag is set. |
| **DR-1741 Is Structural Proof** | A claim evidence is considered a structural proof if at least one of the following holds: all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “Table” and the table has rows flag is set or all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “Field”; the field catalog name has a value; and the field has data flag is set. |
| **DR-1742 Is Question Proof** | A claim evidence is considered a question proof if all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “RoleQuestion”; the question is answered flag is set; and the question witnessed answer has a value. |
| **DR-1743 Is Standard Proof** | A claim evidence is considered a standard proof if at least one of the following holds: all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “OntologyProfile” and the profile mapping count is greater than 0 or all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “KnowledgeMethod” and the method is applied flag is set. |
| **DR-1744 Is Scenario Proof** | A claim evidence is considered a scenario proof if all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “Procedure” and the procedure execution count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1745 Is Valid** | A claim evidence is considered valid if all of the following hold: the justification flag is set and at least one of the following holds: all of the following hold: at least one of the following holds: the claim kind is “Prescription” or the claim kind is “Illustration” and the witness proof flag is set; all of the following hold: the claim kind is “Concept” and the structural proof flag is set; all of the following hold: the claim kind is “CompetencyQuestion” and the question proof flag is set; all of the following hold: the claim kind is “Standard” and the standard proof flag is set; or all of the following hold: the claim kind is “Scenario” and the scenario proof flag is set. |
| **DR-1746 Is Contested** | A claim evidence is considered contested if all of the following hold: the evidence kind is “Field” and the field is contested flag is set. |
| **DR-1747 Is Agreed Evidence** | A claim evidence is considered an agreed evidence if all of the following hold: the valid flag is set and the is contested is false. |
| **DR-1748 Name** | A method application's name is computed as the knowledge method, followed by “ applied: ”, followed by the first 50 character(s) of the applied to. |
| **DR-1749 Name** | A lifecycle status's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1750 Version Use Count** | A lifecycle status's version use count is the number of procedure versions related to the lifecycle status. |
| **DR-1751 Execution Use Count** | A lifecycle status's execution use count is the number of procedure executions related to the lifecycle status. |
| **DR-1752 Is Non Pko Status in Use** | A lifecycle status is considered a non pko status in use if all of the following hold: the is pko status is false and the version use count plus the execution use count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1753 Name** | A facility's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1754 Deviating Run Count** | A facility's deviating run count is the number of procedure executions related to the facility. |
| **DR-1755 Clean Run Count** | A facility's clean run count is the number of procedure executions related to the facility. |
| **DR-1756 Is Deviation Only Facility** | A facility is considered a deviation only facility if all of the following hold: the deviating run count is greater than 0 and the clean run count is 0. |
| **DR-1757 Name** | A machine type's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1758 Name** | An energy source's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1759 Name** | A machine's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1760 Energy Source Count** | A machine's energy source count is the number of machine energy sources related to the machine. |
| **DR-1761 Unisolated Energy Source Count** | A machine's unisolated energy source count is the number of machine energy sources related to the machine. |
| **DR-1762 Is Non Standard Configuration** | A machine is considered a non standard configuration if the configuration kind is “NonStandard”. |
| **DR-1763 Has Unisolated Energy Source** | A machine is considered to have an unisolated energy source if the unisolated energy source count is greater than 0. |
| **DR-1764 Name** | A machine energy source's name is computed as the machine, followed by “ / ”, followed by the energy source. |
| **DR-1765 Machine Procedure Version** | A machine energy source's machine procedure version is the governing procedure version of the machine energy source's machine. |
| **DR-1766 Isolation Step Count** | A machine energy source's isolation step count is the number of steps related to the machine energy source. |
| **DR-1767 Is Unisolated Energy Source** | A machine energy source is considered an unisolated energy source if the isolation step count is 0. |
| **DR-1768 Unisolated Machine Key** | The machine energy source's unisolated machine key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the machine, if the unisolated energy source flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1769 Name** | A lock device's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1770 Name** | A protective equipment's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1771 Name** | A step lock requirement's name is computed as the step, followed by “ / ”, followed by the lock device. |
| **DR-1772 Name** | A step protective equipment's name is computed as the step, followed by “ / ”, followed by the protective equipment. |
| **DR-1773 Name** | A regulatory framework's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1774 Requirement Count** | A regulatory framework's requirement count is the number of requirements related to the regulatory framework. |
| **DR-1775 Required Procedure Count** | A regulatory framework's required procedure count is the number of procedures related to the regulatory framework. |
| **DR-1776 Name** | A procedure target's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1777 Machine is Non Standard** | A procedure target's machine is non standard is true when the procedure target's machine is a non standard configuration. |
| **DR-1778 Handling Failure Mode Count** | A procedure target's handling failure mode count is the number of failure modes related to the procedure target. |
| **DR-1779 Is Unhandled Non Standard Target** | A procedure target is considered an unhandled non standard target if all of the following hold: the machine is non standard flag is set and the handling failure mode count is 0. |
| **DR-1780 Name** | A procedure adoption's name is computed as the organization, followed by “ adopts ”, followed by the procedure. |
| **DR-1781 Is Adoption Mode Unstated** | A procedure adoption is considered adoption-mode-unstated if the adoption mode is blank. |
| **DR-1782 Name** | A procedure outcome criteria's name is computed as the procedure, followed by a space, followed by the polarity. |
| **DR-1783 Failure Procedure Key** | The procedure outcome criteria's failure procedure key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the procedure, if the polarity is “Failure”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1784 Name** | A relation type's name is the same as its label. |
| **DR-1785 Usage Count** | A relation type's usage count is the number of activity relations related to the relation type. |
| **DR-1786 Name** | An activity relation's name is computed as the from step, followed by a space, followed by the relation type, followed by a space, followed by the to step. |
| **DR-1787 Relation Type is Defined** | An activity relation's relation type is defined when the linked relation type is defined. |
| **DR-1788 Uses Undefined Relation Type** | An activity relation is considered to use an undefined relation type if the relation type is defined is false. |
| **DR-1789 From Step Version** | An activity relation's from step version is the procedure version of the activity relation's from step. |
| **DR-1790 Overlaps Version Key** | The activity relation's overlaps version key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the from step version, if the relation type is “Overlaps”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1791 Enables Version Key** | The activity relation's enables version key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the from step version, if the relation type is “Enables”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1792 Prevents Version Key** | The activity relation's prevents version key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the from step version, if the relation type is “Prevents”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1793 Name** | A step variable's name is computed as the step, followed by a space, followed by the direction, followed by a space, followed by the label. |
| **DR-1794 Source Direction** | A step variable's source direction — taken from the linked source variable. |
| **DR-1795 Source Step** | A step variable's source step — taken from the linked source variable. |
| **DR-1796 Is Dangling Input** | A step variable is considered a dangling input if all of the following hold: the direction is “Input”; the source variable is blank; and the is external input is false. |
| **DR-1797 Is Miswired Source** | A step variable is considered a miswired source if all of the following hold: the source variable has a value and the source direction is not “Output”. |
| **DR-1798 Consumer Count** | A step variable's consumer count is the number of step variables related to the step variable. |
| **DR-1799 Input Step Key** | The step variable's input step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the direction is “Input”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1800 Output Step Key** | The step variable's output step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the direction is “Output”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1801 Step Accountable Agent** | A step variable's step accountable agent — taken from the linked step. |
| **DR-1802 Step Agent Kind** | A step variable's step agent kind is the assigned agent kind of the step variable's step. |
| **DR-1803 Consumer Role** | A step variable's consumer role is the assigned role of the step variable's step. |
| **DR-1804 Consumer Workflow** | A step variable's consumer workflow is the procedure version of the step variable's step. |
| **DR-1805 Source Step Agent** | A step variable's source step agent is the accountable agent of the step variable's source step. |
| **DR-1806 Source Step Agent Kind** | A step variable's source step agent kind is the assigned agent kind of the step variable's source step. |
| **DR-1807 Is Input From Ai Artifact** | A step variable is considered an input from ai artifact if all of the following hold: the direction is “Input” and the source step agent kind is “AIAgent”. |
| **DR-1808 Ai Artifact Consumer Has No Accountable Agent** | A step variable is flagged ai artifact consumer has no accountable agent if all of the following hold: the input from ai artifact flag is set and the step accountable agent is blank. |
| **DR-1809 Ai Blast Radius Path** | The step variable's ai blast radius path is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the source step agent, followed by “ produces ”, followed by the label, followed by “ for ”, followed by the step, followed by “; role ”, followed by the consumer role, followed by “; agent ”, followed by the step accountable agent, followed by “; workflow ”, followed by the consumer workflow, if the input from ai artifact flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1810 Name** | An execution entity's name is computed as the step execution, followed by a space, followed by the usage, followed by a space, followed by the entity label. |
| **DR-1811 Variable Direction** | An execution entity's variable direction — taken from the linked step variable. |
| **DR-1812 Variable Step** | An execution entity's variable step — taken from the linked step variable. |
| **DR-1813 Executed Step** | An execution entity's executed step — taken from the linked step execution. |
| **DR-1814 Is Usage Direction Mismatch** | An execution entity is considered an usage direction mismatch if at least one of the following holds: all of the following hold: the usage is “Used” and the variable direction is not “Input” or all of the following hold: the usage is “Generated” and the variable direction is not “Output”. |
| **DR-1815 Is Foreign Variable** | An execution entity is considered foreign-variable if the variable step is not the executed step. |
| **DR-1816 Used Execution Key** | The execution entity's used execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step execution, if the usage is “Used”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1817 Generated Execution Key** | The execution entity's generated execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step execution, if the usage is “Generated”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1818 Variable Datatype** | An execution entity's variable datatype — taken from the linked step variable. |
| **DR-1819 Variable Expected Format** | An execution entity's variable expected format — taken from the linked step variable. |
| **DR-1820 Violates Declared Datatype or Format** | An execution entity is considered to violate a declared datatype or format if at least one of the following holds: all of the following hold: the recorded datatype has a value and the recorded datatype is not the variable datatype or all of the following hold: the recorded format has a value; the variable expected format has a value; and the recorded format is not the variable expected format. |
| **DR-1821 Generating Agent** | An execution entity's generating agent is the executed by agent of the execution entity's step execution. |
| **DR-1822 Attributed to Agent** | The execution entity's attributed to agent is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the generating agent, if the usage is “Generated”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1823 Name** | A step condition's name is computed as the step, followed by a space, followed by the condition kind. |
| **DR-1824 Check Count** | A step condition's check count is the number of condition checks related to the step condition. |
| **DR-1825 Is Never Checked** | A step condition is considered never-checked if the check count is 0. |
| **DR-1826 Precondition Step Key** | The step condition's precondition step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the condition kind is “Precondition”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1827 Postcondition Step Key** | The step condition's postcondition step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the condition kind is “Postcondition”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1828 Invariant Step Key** | The step condition's invariant step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the condition kind is “Invariant”;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1829 Safety Critical Step Key** | The step condition's safety critical step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the safety critical flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1830 Is Machine Parseable** | A step condition is considered machine-parseable if the machine expression has a value. |
| **DR-1831 Name** | A condition check's name is computed as the step execution, followed by “ / ”, followed by the step condition. |
| **DR-1832 Condition Kind** | A condition check's condition kind — taken from the linked step condition. |
| **DR-1833 Is Failed Precondition** | A condition check is considered a failed precondition if all of the following hold: the condition kind is “Precondition” and the held is false. |
| **DR-1834 Is Violated Invariant** | A condition check is considered violated-invariant if all of the following hold: the condition kind is “Invariant” and the held is false. |
| **DR-1835 Failed Precondition Execution Key** | The condition check's failed precondition execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step execution, if the failed precondition flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1836 Violated Invariant Execution Key** | The condition check's violated invariant execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step execution, if the violated invariant flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1837 Name** | A failure mode's name is computed as the step, followed by “: ”, followed by the first 40 character(s) of the description. |
| **DR-1838 Escalation Role Has No Holder** | A failure mode's escalation role has no holder is true when the failure mode's escalate to role has no current holder. |
| **DR-1839 Escalates to Vacant Role** | A failure mode is considered to escalate to vacant role if all of the following hold: the requires escalation flag is set and the escalation role has no holder flag is set. |
| **DR-1840 Has No Response** | A failure mode is considered to have no response if the response is blank. |
| **DR-1841 Name** | A step cue's name is computed as the step, followed by a space, followed by the cue kind. |
| **DR-1842 Observation Count** | A step cue's observation count is the number of cue observations related to the step cue. |
| **DR-1843 Unescalated Observation Count** | A step cue's unescalated observation count is the number of cue observations related to the step cue. |
| **DR-1844 Danger Cue Step Key** | The step cue's danger cue step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the requires escalation flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1845 Incomplete Cue Step Key** | The step cue's incomplete cue step key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step, if the signals incomplete step flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1846 Failure Mode Response** | A step cue's failure mode response — taken from the linked signals failure mode. |
| **DR-1847 Is Unanswerable Sign** | A step cue is considered an unanswerable sign if all of the following hold: the signals incomplete step is true and the signals failure mode is blank. |
| **DR-1848 Name** | A cue observation's name is computed as the step execution, followed by “ / ”, followed by the step cue. |
| **DR-1849 Cue Requires Escalation** | A cue observation's cue requires escalation when the linked step cue requires escalation. |
| **DR-1850 Is Unescalated Danger Cue** | A cue observation is considered an unescalated danger cue if all of the following hold: the cue requires escalation flag is set and the was escalated is false. |
| **DR-1851 Unescalated Cue Key** | The cue observation's unescalated cue key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step cue, if the unescalated danger cue flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1852 Unescalated Execution Key** | The cue observation's unescalated execution key is determined by the following priority:<br>1. the step execution, if the unescalated danger cue flag is set;<br>2. in all other cases, an empty string. |
| **DR-1853 Owner Organization** | A cue observation's owner organization — taken from the linked step execution. |
| **DR-1854 Cue Signals Incomplete Step** | A cue observation's cue signals incomplete step when the linked step cue is signals incomplete step. |
| **DR-1855 Is Awaiting Acknowledgement** | A cue observation is considered awaiting-acknowledgement if all of the following hold: the was escalated is true and the acknowledged at is blank. |
| **DR-1856 Name** | A decision point's name is computed as the step, followed by “: ”, followed by the first 50 character(s) of the question. |
| **DR-1857 Has No Deciding Factors** | A decision point is considered to have no deciding factors if the deciding factors is blank. |
| **DR-1858 Is Dmn Encoded** | A decision point is considered dmn-encoded if the dmn decision key has a value. |
| **DR-1859 Name** | An execution participant's name is computed as the procedure execution, followed by “ / ”, followed by the agent. |
| **DR-1860 Name** | A step resource's name is computed as the step, followed by “ / ”, followed by the resource. |
